claims.claim: SGLang documents dynamic batch size as a source of nondeterministic GPU reduction order because floating-point addition is non-associative.

The documented deterministic inference attention backends are FlashInfer, FlashAttention 3 and Triton, with different feature compatibility for CUDA Graph, chunked prefill, Radix Cache and non-greedy sampling.
SGLang enables deterministic inference through batch-invariant operations and provides tests for varying batch sizes, prefix lengths and Radix Cache consistency.
Batch-invariant operators are implemented in a dedicated SGLang module adapted from Thinking Machines Lab batch_invariant_ops.
claims.locator: Batch invariant operations module and kernel implementation

claims.claim: LLM-42 proposes a decode–verify–rollback mechanism to enforce deterministic inference while retaining fast kernels for non-deterministic decode.
Vosti formalizes system-level deterministic inference across batching, prompt chunking and KV cache reuse/eviction, and reports counterexamples in production modes.
Deterministic inference can reduce rollout variation but does not alone prove training and inference use identical kernels, weights or sampler state.
claims.locator: LLM-42 project motivation and SGLang integration notes; training parity is a separate system contract
